skill.name: paper-2-web
skill.description: Guides conversion of academic papers into interactive websites, presentation videos, and conference posters using Paper2All workflows.
skill.summary: Turn research papers into web, video, and poster presentation assets.
skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: The review confirmed a privileged package installation step and network-based setup from a third-party repository. Most scanner matches are false positives from Markdown code fences, placeholder API key names, .env documentation, or normal quality-review prose. No prompt injection attempt, credential exfiltration instruction, or hidden malicious behavior was found in the reviewed files.

remediation.suggestion: Mark sudo package installation as a manual confirmation step and provide non-sudo installation alternatives where possible.
Pin Paper2All to a release or commit and document dependency verification before running pipeline scripts.
State that .env credentials must stay local and should never be pasted into prompts, screenshots, or shared outputs.

content.user_title: Transform Papers into Web, Video, and Posters
content.value_statement: Academic papers are hard to reuse across websites, posters, and videos. This skill guides Paper2All workflows that turn papers into presentation-ready assets.
actual_capabilities: Guides Paper2Web creation of responsive academic homepages from papers.
Documents Paper2Video workflows for slides, narration, subtitles, and final video files.
Documents Paper2Poster workflows for print-ready conference posters.
Explains input preparation for LaTeX sources, PDFs, figures, tables, and bibliography files.
Provides workflow examples for single papers, batches, posters, and video abstracts.
limitations: Requires a separate Paper2All installation and its Python dependencies.
Uses API keys for LLM providers and optional Google logo search.
Talking-head video generation requires high-end NVIDIA GPU hardware.
Generated websites, videos, and posters need human review for scientific accuracy.

use_cases.title: Create a Research Homepage
use_cases.description: Convert a preprint or published paper into a responsive companion website with figures and citations.

use_cases.title: Prepare Conference Materials
use_cases.description: Generate a poster and presentation video from LaTeX sources before a poster session or talk.

use_cases.title: Publish Lab Outputs
use_cases.description: Batch prepare websites for multiple papers so a lab can share recent work consistently.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Paper Website
prompt_templates.prompt: Convert the paper in [paper folder] into an interactive website. Use the available figures and include mobile-friendly navigation.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a Conference Poster
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a print-ready poster from [paper folder]. Use [poster size] and highlight the main findings, methods, and contact details.

prompt_templates.title: Generate a Video Abstract
prompt_templates.prompt: Generate a [duration] video abstract for this paper. Keep the narration accessible and emphasize the key results and figures.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Full Dissemination Package
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a website, poster, and presentation video from [paper folder]. Match the visual style across all outputs and list review steps.

output_examples.input: A LaTeX paper prepared for a machine learning conference.
output_examples.output: A companion website, a print-ready poster, and a presentation video organized in separate output folders.

output_examples.input: A PDF preprint without LaTeX source files.
output_examples.output: A responsive research homepage with abstract, key findings, figure sections, author details, and reference links.

output_examples.input: A journal submission that needs a short multimedia summary.
output_examples.output: A concise video abstract with generated slides, narration, subtitles, and a final review checklist.

best_practices: Use clean LaTeX sources with all figures, tables, and bibliography files present.
Review every generated asset for scientific accuracy before publishing or printing.
Keep API keys local and avoid placing credentials in prompts, screenshots, or shared outputs.
anti_patterns: Do not rely on generated text for claims that were not present in the paper.
Do not print posters before checking dimensions, readability, colors, and QR codes.
Do not enable talking-head video unless the required GPU and presenter permissions are available.

faq.question: What input formats does this skill support?
faq.answer: It supports LaTeX source directories and high-quality PDFs with selectable text and clear figures.

faq.question: Can it create only a website?
faq.answer: Yes. The workflow can focus on Paper2Web without generating poster or video outputs.

faq.question: Does it require API keys?
faq.answer: Yes. Paper2All uses LLM provider keys, and logo search can require Google API credentials.

faq.question: Is a GPU required?
faq.answer: A GPU is optional for standard outputs, but talking-head video generation needs a large NVIDIA GPU.

faq.question: Can it process several papers?
faq.answer: Yes. The documentation includes batch workflows for multiple papers in organized input folders.

faq.question: Are outputs ready to publish without review?
faq.answer: No. Users should verify content accuracy, figure quality, links, accessibility, and print settings.
